attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: The normalised wording keeps 'predominantly', 'seem incapable', and the clause allowing that some companies find product-market fit. The checkable core, that most of these companies were unprofitable, is a present-tense observation.

contract.note: Reading 'predominantly' as more than half and 'unprofitable' as negative net income is ordinary and fair. Treating the hedged valuation judgment as not separately scored is fair to his words. The population is loosely defined, but that does not decide the result here.

evidence.note: Anthropic's S-1 (available 2026-10-26, before the cutoff) reports an $8.3B net loss for 2024. That is one loss-making company in the population. It cannot establish the share of companies losing money.

A July 2025 report says Surge AI has been profitable since inception, with no figure or accounting definition given. It is a single exception, and Surge, a data-labelling firm, sits at the edge of the population. It cannot contradict a majority claim.

reviews.rationale: The contract needs comparable net-income results for most of the relevant companies. The packet has one audited loss (Anthropic) and one reported profitable exception (Surge AI). It sets no population and gives no profit status for most of the named firms. The evidence available by the cutoff therefore cannot show whether more than half were unprofitable.
